clue.text: Yes, European is in more than one way leaking a gallon, but it does what it says on the tin

definitions.text: it does what it says on the tin

indicators.note: the European yes is placed inside the doubled, trimmed word for a way
more than one way means the trimmed word is written twice over
leaking means the letter a drips out of the word for way

parts.note: way gives WAY, a route
si is yes in Spanish and Italian, so a European yes

explanation.surface: A rambling complaint about a European agreement and a leaky can that still lives up to its label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaking a' takes A out of WAY, 'more than one' writes the result twice, and 'is in' puts SI between the copies. The definition is a British advertising slogan for a product that is exactly as labelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The computing acronym for a display matching printed output is glossed by the British advertising slogan about honest product labels.

clue.text: Supple women, somewhat broad in the beam?

parts.note: hippy means having large hips, broad in the beam

explanation.surface: A remark about women who are flexible but a little wide around the hips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad in the beam' is a colloquial way of saying wide-hipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible and springy, like a cane that bends easily, is supple.

clue.text: More oblique kind of pin

definitions.meaning: skew means slanting, so the comparative means more slanting
a pointed pin or rod used to hold meat for cooking

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of skew means more slanted, and the noun is a long pin for holding food on a grill.

clue.text: Is now off, presumably, after crushing night out for one of the 11 seen on 26 17

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing something in between, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: something that is now off presumably was on before

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something has stopped working after a crushing night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NIGHT to HINGT and 'crushing' squeezes it between WAS and ON; 'after' is a link. Something now switched off presumably was on before.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington, the first US president, is one of four presidents carved into Mount Rushmore.

clue.text: Quick steps taken up by old English soldier

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means read upwards, so the word for quick steps is reversed

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance of quick steps

explanation.surface: An old English soldier learning a quick dance.
explanation.walkthrough: G.I. Joe is slang for an American private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an ordinary enlisted American serviceman, after the government issue designation.

clue.text: One's put out as is the victim of ambush

indicators.note: put out suggests something disturbed or displaced, so the letters of the first words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone displaced and inconvenienced, like a person caught in an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: To be attacked suddenly and violently is to be assailed; the phrase describes a person who suffered that assault.

clue.text: In emergency one catches banker in movable feast

indicators.note: in places the river inside the rearranged letters
movable means the letters can be shifted around into a new order

parts.note: a banker is something with banks, a river; the Tyne flows through Newcastle

explanation.surface: Someone catching a banker during an emergency at a Church festival such as Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movable' rearranges FEAST to SAFET and 'in' sets TYNE within it. A movable feast is a church festival with no fixed date, like Easter; a banker is a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A net under acrobats catches anyone who falls, an emergency safeguard.

clue.text: Man or woman representing Wagner opus?

indicators.note: representing means one thing stands for another: the ring in the opera title is shown by a ring-shaped letter

parts.note: Wagner's great operatic cycle is known in English as The Ring

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a male or female figure stands for a Wagner opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring-shaped letter O stands in for RING in the opera's title.
explanation.definitionFit: This short name can belong to a man, as Theodore, or to a woman, as Theodora.

clue.text: Matter to brood over? I'm easily persuaded

parts.note: pus is purulent matter from a wound
to hover over something is to linger above it, as a bird broods over its nest

explanation.surface: Someone saying a matter to ponder will easily win them round.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives hover as to brood over, as a hen does.
explanation.definitionFit: A person easily persuaded or defeated is a soft touch, someone with little resistance.

clue.text: Make love with nurses in bunk

indicators.note: in places the nurses inside the word for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so none
SENs are State Enrolled Nurses

explanation.surface: Having sex with nurses in a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed but is the definition: rubbish. A State Enrolled Nurse was a British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is short for bunkum, meaning foolish talk or rubbish.

clue.text: It causes pain when food course is delayed

definitions.text: It causes pain when food course is delayed

parts.words: It causes pain when food course is delayed
parts.note: food course suggests a meal's next dish arriving late, but it means the passage of food through the gut being blocked

explanation.surface: A grumble about a restaurant serving its next dish too slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'food course' is the route food takes through the intestines, not a dish in a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term names a painful intestinal obstruction in which digested matter stops moving along the bowel.

clue.text: Airplane of note — one of the 11 seen on 26 17

definitions.meaning: ... Airplane was a famous American rock band
one of the presidents carved on Mount Rushmore

explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' hints at music: the band Jefferson Airplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the name of a well-known psychedelic rock group and belongs to the third US president.

clue.text: VIPs' private parking?

parts.note: read as P for parking followed by the word for people with private resident parking spaces

explanation.surface: A sign reserving parking spaces for important people.
explanation.walkthrough: P is parking, followed by RESIDENTS, whose parking is private; the whole names important people.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of state and company chiefs are very important people, so the plural noun fits the VIPs.

clue.text: The first notes of a French artist

parts.note: do is the first note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The opening bars of a piece by a painter from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustave Doré was a nineteenth-century French illustrator and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Doré was a celebrated French illustrator, best known for his Bible and Dante engravings.

clue.text: Baker buttonholed by milliner who does unpleasant work?

indicators.note: to be buttonholed is to be held fast, here held inside the milliner

parts.note: a milliner makes hats, a hat man
Chet Baker was an American jazz trumpeter

explanation.surface: A baker accosted by a hat maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person hired to do dirty jobs such as firings or character attacks is an enforcer of that kind.

clue.text: Do they bear the intentions of the government's eco-press?

definitions.text: Do they bear the intentions of the government's

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, which is green
the press is the newspapers, the papers

explanation.surface: A question about whether an environmentally minded newspaper carries the government's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a consultation document setting out proposed government policy is called a Green Paper.
explanation.definitionFit: British consultative documents set out policy proposals the government intends, before any firm commitment.

clue.text: In film lost climbing personnel sign up for this!

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word for lost and the staff inside the film's title

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word for lost is reversed

parts.note: lorn means forlorn, lost
personnel are staff, men

explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns LORN backwards to NROL, as the clue reads up the grid; 'In' sets it and MEN within ET, the Spielberg film.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up is joining a register, so the noun names the act of registering membership.

clue.text: Bring muscle into play on guitar range

indicators.note: into puts the muscle inside the word for playing the guitar

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings
a pec is a pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A guitarist putting muscle into playing across the instrument's range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range or sweep of things, as of colours or opinions.

clue.text: See 26
Planet, very cold, with over half of the rich in power

parts.note: Pluto was classed as a planet until 2006

indicators.note: over means turned back, and half limits that turning to the first half of the word for very cold

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold

explanation.surface: A frozen distant world combined with more than half of a wealthy ruling class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with over half' reverses only the first half of ARCTIC, ARC becoming CRA while TIC stays put. Pluto was still called a planet when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocracy is government by the wealthy, so this adjective describes rule by the rich.

clue.text: It's driven us round for a tenner, as quoted

parts.note: a car is something that is driven
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A taxi taking us round town for a ten pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tenner, as quoted' means the word tenor when spoken: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian tenor. A tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the great Italian operatic tenor, and a tenner said out loud gives the singer's voice type.

clue.text: Beastly young Christopher Jefferson!

parts.note: Kit is a short form of Christopher
Jefferson is the answer to ten across, so it stands for ten

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a badly behaved young man named Christopher Jefferson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly young' is the definition: a young beast, a young cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is a baby animal, so a beast's young.

clue.text: In business, I say "Pacific salmon"

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
ho is an exclamation used to attract attention, like I say

explanation.surface: A trader announcing a fish from the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a silver salmon species native to the North Pacific and its rivers.

clue.text: Are we wearing gilt attire?

indicators.note: wearing suggests erosion, the letters worn into a new shape

explanation.surface: Celebrities asking whether they are dressed in golden clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable celebrities are the kind of people who might ask whether golden clothing is being worn.

clue.text: Leader of team having a lot to do? The lot

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
to do suggests something to be made or worked on, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A team captain with plenty of work facing everything at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do' rearranges A LOT into OTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole amount, everything taken together, is the lot.

clue.text: Twit Micawber knew to be in hiding

indicators.note: the answer is concealed within the run of the words Micawber knew

explanation.surface: The Dickens character Micawber knowing an idiot would hide away.
explanation.walkthrough: Berk is British slang for a fool; Micawber is the optimistic debtor in David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Berk is mild British slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Resolve to convert one of the 11 (6 12) seen on 26 17

explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt, the twenty-sixth US president, is one of the four faces carved on the South Dakota mountain.

clue.text: A whip could make this a place where famous faces appear

parts.note: read as a phrase; also a mountain carved with presidents' faces

clue.text: Animal, always poetically grand, seen sprawling across rug

K is slang for a thousand, a grand
